1→# Ryde — Multi-Agent Autonomous Dispute Resolution
   2→
   3→Entry for the **Tencent Cloud "AI CAN DO IT" Hackathon Singapore 2026**, Digital Native track
   4→(the Ryde challenge statement, section 5 of the organisers' document).
   5→
   6→**Status: the system runs end to end on the real Tencent Cloud model (ADP), with the
   7→deterministic mock as the default for a fresh checkout.** The scope is ruled: a two-category MVP
   8→(route deviation + no-show charge) with three agents, a deterministic evidence layer, and an
   9→observable case-file view. The challenge statement is in
  10→[`docs/statement-extract.md`](docs/statement-extract.md); the builder's contract is in
  11→[`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md).
  12→
  13→## The challenge
  14→
  15→Ride-hailing platforms process thousands of dispute tickets daily: fare disputes, route deviations,
  16→property damage, safety incidents, no-show charges. They are subjective, emotionally charged, and
  17→currently resolved by humans reviewing GPS telemetry, chat logs, payment records and company policy
  18→by hand. The result is slow, expensive and inconsistent.
  19→
  20→The task is an autonomous multi-agent system that gathers evidence, builds both sides' cases, applies
  21→company policy and issues a fair ruling with a confidence score and a plain-language explanation.
  22→
  23→## Architecture
  24→
  25→Three core agents, all MVP-required:
  26→
  27→| Agent | Role |
  28→|---|---|
  29→| **Rider Advocate** | Builds the rider's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  30→| **Driver Advocate** | Builds the driver's case from the Evidence Pack and the policy |
  31→| **Judge** | Weighs both cases, applies policy, rules, and explains the reasoning with a confidence score |
  32→
  33→Inter-agent communication must be **observable** — a judge needs to see how the agents exchange
  34→information and build their cases. That surface is a required deliverable, not a nice-to-have.
  35→
  36→The full walkthrough — components, lifecycle, gates, observability — is in
  37→[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md). The system on one page:

  40→flowchart TD
  41→    PACK["Dataset pack"] --> B["Server"]
  42→    PACK --> CL["Command-line runner"]
  43→    A["Rider and driver intake forms"] --> B
  44→    B --> C{"Category in scope?"}
  45→    CL --> C
  46→    C -- "Out of scope" --> H["Human review"]
  47→    C -- "Route deviation or no-show" --> E["Evidence Pack"]
  48→    POL["Policy document"] --> RA["Rider Advocate"]
  49→    POL --> DA["Driver Advocate"]
  50→    POL --> J["Judge"]
  51→    E --> RA
  52→    E --> DA

  54→    DA --> S

  58→    S -- "No" --> J
  59→    J --> G{"Gates pass? Confidence, cap, measured deviation, NS-6, NS-8, RD-5, RD-4"}
  60→    G -- "Yes" --> O1["Ruled"]
  61→    G -- "No" --> O2["Withheld"]
  62→    O2 -- "Candidate ruling queued" --> H

  64→    B -. "Every step emits an event" .-> L["Event log"]

  73→- [`docs/policy.md`](docs/policy.md) — the policy rule set the Judge applies, with per-rule provenance
  74→- [`docs/dataset.md`](docs/dataset.md) — the labelled corpus, its provenance and its limitations
  75→- [`docs/prompts.md`](docs/prompts.md) — how the prompts drive each agent, and what code checks after the model answers
  76→- [`docs/replay.md`](docs/replay.md) — the static replay of a recorded run: how it is exported and what it shows
  77→- [`docs/evidence-plan.md`](docs/evidence-plan.md) — development-process evidence rules
  78→- [`docs/tool-experiences.md`](docs/tool-experiences.md) — running log of how the development tools behaved
  79→- [`docs/build-briefs/`](docs/build-briefs/) — the brief each CodeBuddy build session worked from, kept as a record of the process
  80→- [`CODEBUDDY.md`](CODEBUDDY.md) — builder's entry point and project memory
  81→
  82→## Development tooling
  83→
  84→Built with Tencent Cloud **CodeBuddy**. The competition mandates proof of product usage, so
  85→development happens in the tool and evidence is captured as it occurs.
  86→
  87→## Run
  88→
  89→No dependencies and no API key needed for a first look: it runs on a stock Python 3.9+ with the
  90→standard library only, using a deterministic mock in place of the LLM.
  91→
  92→To see it in a browser, start the server and open the two pages:
  93→
  94→```bash
  95→python3 -m app.server
  96→```
  97→
  98→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/` is the operator console (case files, the review queue, human decisions)
  99→- `http://127.0.0.1:8000/party/` is the rider's dispute form, which links to the driver form and the status page
 100→
 101→To run the tests and single cases from the command line:
 102→
 103→```bash
 104→python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
 105→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0101
 106→python3 -m app.cli --pack organiser-style-v1 --dispute DISP-002
 107→```
 108→
 109→The evaluation harness replays every labelled case — `python3 -m app.eval --llm tencent --repeat 3` —
 110→and scores the rulings against the labels, answering a round-one stop and running it again.
 111→
 112→`--dispute` takes either a dispute id inside the selected pack or a path to a record file
 113→(`python3 -m app.cli --dispute data/packs/ryde-synth-v1/disputes/RD-0101.json`). The pack
 114→defaults to `dataset_pack` in `app/config.json`; `--pack` overrides it for one run.
 115→
 116→That prints the agent-to-agent event strip and the ruling, and writes the run's artifacts to
 117→`runs/<run_id>/`: `events.jsonl` (the observable traffic), `payloads/*.json` (the full payload
 118→behind each event) and `case_file.json` (evidence, both claims, resolution).
 119→
 120→The rider form is `/party/index.html`; the driver form is `/party/driver-filing.html`.
 121→Both use the shared form script and the same filing API. Save the reference number for
 122→`/party/status.html#reference-input`, which recovers questions and the current outcome.
 123→The rider demo list contains rider filings only. The read-only driver account at
 124→`/party/driver.html` is fixed to D-2009, including T-RD0109; filings on other sample drivers'
 125→trips need reference lookup and do not appear in that account. The forms are local demos,
 126→not signed-in accounts. Entering an amount is a request, not a payment.
 127→
 128→The corpus lives in two swappable packs under `data/packs/`: `ryde-synth-v1` (our 17 labelled
 129→cases, our record shape) and `organiser-style-v1` (the same 17 cases as twins in the organisers'
 130→shape, plus the organisers' own `DISP-002` verbatim). `RD-0103` is a deviation too small to
 131→matter, `NS-0203` is a driver who marked arrival 885 m from the pickup point, `RD-0109` is a
 132→remedy above the autonomous cap that the system refuses to issue on its own, and `OS-0301` is an
 133→out-of-scope filing routed to human review without an LLM call. `docs/dataset.md` maps each case
 134→to what it tests; `<pack>/ground-truth.json` holds the expected outcomes, deliberately kept out
 135→of the records the agents see.
 136→
 137→Seven gates stand between a ruling and the parties, and **all seven are enforced in Python, not
 138→asked of the model in a prompt**: the confidence threshold, ESC-4's SGD 50 autonomous cap, ESC-2,
 139→which withholds a route-case ruling when the deviation cannot be measured or the fare charged
 140→cannot be established, NS-6, which withholds a
 141→contested no-show unless the ruling is a refund of exactly the fee for a low fee and a clean rider
 142→record, NS-8, which withholds a no-show refund larger than the recorded fee, any compensation on a
 143→no-show case, or any refund whose fee the record cannot prove, RD-5, which withholds a route ruling
 144→that refunds less than the overcharge the records prove, and RD-4, which withholds a route refund
 145→larger than the records prove the rider overpaid (a fixed fare paid as quoted proves nothing) and
 146→any compensation on a route case. Each gate withholds the ruling for a human; none of them rewrites
 147→what the Judge proposed.
 148→Try them:
 149→
 150→```bash
 151→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0109   # withheld: above the cap
 152→python3 -m app.cli --pack ryde-synth-v1 --dispute RD-0108   # withheld: no deviation to measure
 153→```
 154→
 155→**Mock by default.** The default provider is a deterministic mock. Its free-text fields (claim
 156→summaries, arguments, the Judge's explanation) are prefixed `MOCK`; actions, amounts, rule IDs and
 157→evidence refs are not. A mock run is a plumbing demonstration, never a real ruling. The real model is
 158→Tencent Cloud ADP, one app per agent: put the three app keys in `.env` (see `.env.example`), then
 159→run `python3 -m app.server --llm tencent` or `python3 -m app.cli --llm tencent --dispute <id>`.
 160→
 161→## How this was built
 162→
 163→The code in `app/` and `ui/` was written in Tencent Cloud CodeBuddy. A planning agent wrote each
 164→session's brief and its failing tests first; CodeBuddy built until they passed, and the result was
 165→re-checked by running it, not by describing it. The screenshots in `evidence/` record those
 166→sessions as they happened.

1→"""Runtime configuration: settings from app/config.json, secrets from the environment.
   2→
   3→Split rule (keeps the public repo clean):
   4→  * settings   -> app/config.json   (committed; threshold, provider, paths, dataset pack)
   5→  * secrets    -> .env / environment (never committed; API keys only)
   6→
   7→The dataset pack names which corpus under data/packs/ the CLI reads disputes from;
   8→`resolve_pack_dir` turns the name into a path and refuses an unknown one.
   9→
  10→The confidence threshold is read from config and passed explicitly into the pipeline.
  11→It is never hard-coded in agent logic, so the demo can change it live by editing the
  12→config file and re-running.
  13→
  14→Standard library only: json + a minimal .env reader (python-dotenv is not a dependency
  15→of this project and the .env format we need is three lines long).
  16→"""
  17→
  18→from __future__ import annotations
  19→
  20→import json
  21→import os
  22→from dataclasses import dataclass
  23→from pathlib import Path
  24→from typing import Any, Dict, Optional
  25→
  26→REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
  27→DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "app" / "config.json"
  28→DEFAULT_ENV_PATH = REPO_ROOT / ".env"
  29→
  30→#: Where the swappable dispute corpora live, and which one runs unless config says
  31→#: otherwise. A pack is a directory holding disputes/, ground-truth.json and pack.json;
  32→#: swapping one in is a directory copy, never a code change.
  33→DATASET_PACKS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "data" / "packs"
  34→DEFAULT_DATASET_PACK = "organiser-style-v1"
  35→
  36→
  37→class ConfigError(RuntimeError):
  38→    """Configuration is missing, unreadable or out of range."""
  39→
  40→
  41→# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- .env
  42→
  43→
  44→def load_env_file(path: Optional[Path] = None) -> Dict[str, str]:
  45→    """Read a .env file into a dict. Returns {} when the file does not exist.
  46→
  47→    Accepts `KEY=value`, optional `export ` prefix, `#` comments and single or double
  48→    quoted values. Deliberately minimal — enough for the two variables this project uses.
  49→    """
  50→    env_path = Path(path) if path is not None else DEFAULT_ENV_PATH
  51→    if not env_path.exists():
  52→        return {}
  53→
  54→    values: Dict[str, str] = {}
  55→    for raw_line in env_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
  56→        line = raw_line.strip()
  57→        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
  58→            continue
  59→        if line.startswith("export "):
  60→            line = line[len("export "):].strip()
  61→        if "=" not in line:
  62→            continue
  63→        key, _, value = line.partition("=")
  64→        value = value.strip()
  65→        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in "\"'":
  66→            value = value[1:-1]
  67→        values[key.strip()] = value
  68→    return values
  69→
  70→
  71→def read_secret(name: str, env_path: Optional[Path] = None) -> Optional[str]:
  72→    """Look up a secret: real environment first, then the .env file. None if unset.
  73→
  74→    The environment wins so a shell export can override a stale local file.
  75→    """
  76→    from_environ = os.environ.get(name)
  77→    if from_environ:
  78→        return from_environ
  79→    value = load_env_file(env_path).get(name)
  80→    return value or None
  81→
  82→
  83→# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- config
  84→
  85→
  86→@dataclass(frozen=True)
  87→class LLMSettings:
  88→    """Which provider to call and how. The API key is not here — it is a secret."""
  89→
  90→    provider: str
  91→    endpoint: str
  92→    model: str
  93→    temperature: float
  94→    max_tokens: int
  95→    timeout_seconds: int
  96→    case_budget_seconds: float = 120.0
  97→
  98→
  99→@dataclass(frozen=True)
 100→class Config:
 101→    """Everything the pipeline needs to run one dispute."""
 102→
 103→    confidence_threshold: float
 104→    autonomous_cap_sgd: float
 105→    llm: LLMSettings
 106→    policy_path: Path
 107→    out_dir: Path
 108→    source_path: Path
 109→    #: The dataset pack to read disputes from: its name, and its resolved directory.
 110→    dataset_pack: str
 111→    dataset_pack_dir: Path
 112→
 113→
 114→def _require_mapping(data: Dict[str, Any], key: str, where: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
 115→    value = data.get(key)
 116→    if not isinstance(value, dict):
 117→        raise ConfigError("%s: '%s' must be an object, got %r" % (where, key, value))
 118→    return value
 119→
 120→
 121→def _resolve_path(value: Any, key: str, where: str) -> Path:
 122→    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
 123→        raise ConfigError("%s: paths.%s must be a non-empty string, got %r" % (where, key, value))
 124→    path = Path(value.strip())
 125→    return path if path.is_absolute() else (REPO_ROOT / path).resolve()
 126→
 127→
 128→def _pack_name(value: Any) -> str:
 129→    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
 130→        raise ConfigError("dataset_pack must be a non-empty pack name, got %r" % (value,))
 131→    return value.strip()
 132→
 133→
 134→def resolve_pack_dir(name: str) -> Path:
 135→    """Resolve a dataset pack name to its directory under data/packs/.
 136→
 137→    Raises ConfigError for a name that is not a pack, listing what is available: a run
 138→    against a pack that does not exist must fail before it reads anything, not part-way
 139→    through with a missing dispute file.
 140→    """
 141→    pack_name = _pack_name(name)
 142→    path = (DATASET_PACKS_DIR / pack_name).resolve()
 143→    if not (path / "disputes").is_dir():
 144→        available = ", ".join(sorted(p.name for p in DATASET_PACKS_DIR.glob("*") if (p / "disputes").is_dir()))
 145→        raise ConfigError(
 146→            "unknown dataset pack %r: %s has no disputes/ directory. Available packs: %s"
 147→            % (pack_name, path, available or "(none)")
 148→        )
 149→    return path
 150→
 151→
 152→def load_config(path: Optional[Path] = None) -> Config:
 153→    """Load and validate app/config.json. Raises ConfigError with a readable message."""
 154→    config_path = Path(path) if path is not None else DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH
 155→    if not config_path.exists():
 156→        raise ConfigError("config file not found: %s" % config_path)
 157→    try:
 158→        data = json.loads(config_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
 159→    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
 160→        raise ConfigError("config file is not valid JSON (%s): %s" % (config_path, exc)) from exc
 161→    if not isinstance(data, dict):
 162→        raise ConfigError("config file must contain a JSON object: %s" % config_path)
 163→
 164→    where = str(config_path)
 165→
 166→    threshold = data.get("confidence_threshold")
 167→    if isinstance(threshold, bool) or not isinstance(threshold, (int, float)):
 168→        raise ConfigError("%s: confidence_threshold must be a number, got %r" % (where, threshold))
 169→    threshold = float(threshold)
 170→    if not 0.0 <= threshold <= 1.0:
 171→        raise ConfigError(
 172→            "%s: confidence_threshold must be between 0 and 1, got %r" % (where, threshold)
 173→        )
 174→
 175→    # ESC-4's autonomous decision cap. A remedy above this is prepared but never issued
 176→    # without a human. Defaults to the policy's stated SGD 50.00 when the key is absent,
 177→    # so an older config file cannot silently disable the gate.
 178→    cap = data.get("autonomous_cap_sgd", 50.00)
 179→    if isinstance(cap, bool) or not isinstance(cap, (int, float)):
 180→        raise ConfigError("%s: autonomous_cap_sgd must be a number, got %r" % (where, cap))
 181→    cap = float(cap)
 182→    if cap <= 0.0:
 183→        raise ConfigError(
 184→            "%s: autonomous_cap_sgd must be greater than 0, got %r. A cap of zero or less "
 185→            "would withhold every ruling that moves money." % (where, cap)
 186→        )
 187→
 188→    llm_raw = _require_mapping(data, "llm", where)
 189→    provider = llm_raw.get("provider")
 190→    if not isinstance(provider, str) or not provider.strip():
 191→        raise ConfigError("%s: llm.provider must be a non-empty string" % where)
 192→
 193→    temperature = llm_raw.get("temperature", 0.0)
 194→    if isinstance(temperature, bool) or not isinstance(temperature, (int, float)):
 195→        raise ConfigError("%s: llm.temperature must be a number" % where)
 196→
 197→    max_tokens = llm_raw.get("max_tokens", 1500)
 198→    if isinstance(max_tokens, bool) or not isinstance(max_tokens, int) or max_tokens <= 0:
 199→        raise ConfigError("%s: llm.max_tokens must be a positive integer" % where)
 200→
 201→    timeout = llm_raw.get("timeout_seconds", 60)
 202→    if isinstance(timeout, bool) or not isinstance(timeout, (int, float)) or timeout <= 0:
 203→        raise ConfigError("%s: llm.timeout_seconds must be a positive number" % where)
 204→
 205→    case_budget = llm_raw.get("case_budget_seconds", 120.0)
 206→    if isinstance(case_budget, bool) or not isinstance(case_budget, (int, float)) or case_budget <= 0:
 207→        raise ConfigError("%s: llm.case_budget_seconds must be a positive number" % where)
 208→
 209→    paths_raw = _require_mapping(data, "paths", where)
 210→    policy_path = _resolve_path(paths_raw.get("policy"), "policy", where)
 211→    out_dir = _resolve_path(paths_raw.get("out_dir"), "out_dir", where)
 212→
 213→    # Which corpus to run on. Defaulted rather than required, so a config file written
 214→    # before the packs existed still loads and still names a real pack.
 215→    pack_name = _pack_name(data.get("dataset_pack", DEFAULT_DATASET_PACK))

 217→
 218→    llm = LLMSettings(
 219→        provider=provider.strip(),
 220→        endpoint=str(llm_raw.get("endpoint", "") or ""),
 221→        model=str(llm_raw.get("model", "") or ""),
 222→        temperature=float(temperature),
 223→        max_tokens=int(max_tokens),
 224→        timeout_seconds=int(timeout),
 225→        case_budget_seconds=float(case_budget),
 226→    )
 227→
 228→    return Config(
 229→        confidence_threshold=threshold,
 230→        autonomous_cap_sgd=cap,
 231→        llm=llm,
 232→        policy_path=policy_path,
 233→        out_dir=out_dir,
 234→        source_path=config_path.resolve(),
 235→        dataset_pack=pack_name,
 236→        dataset_pack_dir=pack_dir,
 237→    )

{"file_path": "[USER_HOME]/hermes-workspace/projects/ryde-build-worktrees/w34-launcher/tools/launch.py", "content": """"One-click launcher for the Ryde demo.

Double-clicked through start.command (macOS) or start.bat (Windows), or run by hand:

    python3 tools/launch.py [--ports FIRST-LAST]

The launcher picks the first free port in the range — reusing a Ryde demo that is
already running — then runs the EXISTING app.server entry point in this same process
with the mock provider, and opens the start page once the server answers. One process
is load-bearing: Ctrl+C reaches app.server's own KeyboardInterrupt handler, and
closing the terminal window (SIGHUP) ends the process and frees the port.

This is a helper for the demo, not part of the app: app/ and ui/ never import it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import socket
import sys
import threading
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import webbrowser
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Tuple

#: Run as `python3 tools/launch.py`, sys.path[0] is tools/, so the repository root
#: goes in before app.server is imported. The launcher never re-implements server
#: startup; it calls the existing entry point.
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

import app.server as server  # noqa: E402 - sys.path is prepared just above

FIRST_PORT = 8000
LAST_PORT = 8010
START_PATH = "/start/"

#: How long one probe may wait for an answer: a listener that accepts the connection
#: but never speaks must not stall the launcher.
PROBE_TIMEOUT = 1.0
#: The browser waiter's polling cadence, and how long it waits for the server to
#: answer before printing the URL instead.
POLL_SECONDS = 0.1
READY_TIMEOUT = 30.0

#: The banner app/server.py sends. A 200 carrying it is the only proof that a port
#: serves this demo and not some other program.
SERVER_HEADER = "RydePartyServer/"

RUNNING = "Ryde demo running at {url}"
STOP_HINT = "Close this window (or press Ctrl+C) to stop the demo."
ALREADY_RUNNING = "The Ryde demo is already running at {url}. Opening it in your browser."
NO_FREE_PORT = ("Ports {first} to {last} are all in use by other programs. "
                "Close one of them, then open this file again.")
OPEN_YOURSELF = "Could not open a browser. Open {url} yourself."


def start_url(port: int) -> str:
    """The start page's URL on 127.0.0.1."""
    return "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (port, START_PATH)


def server_argv(port: int) -> list:
    """The existing server's own arguments: the mock, and the chosen port."""
    return ["--llm", "mock", "--port", str(port)]


def _answer(url: str) -> Optional[Tuple[int, str]]:
    """(status, Server header) for a GET, or None when the port did not answer.

    Any failure to get an answer — refused, timed out, a listener that speaks
    something that is not HTTP — reads as None, never as a status.
    """
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=PROBE_TIMEOUT) as response:
            return response.status, response.headers.get("Server", "")
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        return exc.code, exc.headers.get("Server", "")
    except Exception:
        return None


def is_ryde_demo(port: int) -> bool:
    """True only when GET /start/ answers 200 with the Ryde server banner.

    Nothing listening, another program's 200, and the Ryde banner on a 404 are all
    False: only the two together prove this port serves the demo.
    """
    answer = _answer(start_url(port))
    return bool(answer and answer[0] == 200 and answer[1].startswith(SERVER_HEADER))


def _is_free(port: int) -> bool:
    """True when a TCP connect to 127.0.0.1:port is refused (nobody is listening)."""
    try:
        with socket.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port), timeout=PROBE_TIMEOUT):
            return False
    except ConnectionRefusedError:
        return True
    except OSError:
        # Not a refusal — something is there, or the probe could not tell. Skipping
        # the port is the safe reading.
        return False


def pick_port(first: int, last: int) -> Tuple[Optional[int], bool]:
    """The first usable port in [first, last], and whether the demo already runs on it.

    Ports are walked in order. A port already serving the Ryde demo is reused. Any
    other listener — HTTP or one that never answers — is skipped. The first port
    whose TCP connect is refused is used. (None, False) when every port is taken.
    """
    for port in range(first, last + 1):
        if is_ryde_demo(port):
            return port, True
        if _is_free(port):
            return port, False
    return None, False


def _open(url: str) -> bool:
    """Open url in the default browser. False when the browser refused or raised."""
    try:
        return bool(webbrowser.open(url))
    except webbrowser.Error:
        return False


def open_when_ready(url: str, timeout: float = READY_TIMEOUT) -> None:
    """Open url in the browser once it answers 200, or print it when that fails.

    The server starts on the main thread after this waiter, so the page must not be
    opened before the port answers. A server that never answers, and a browser that
    refuses or raises, both print the URL so the demo is still reachable by hand.
    """
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while True:
        answer = _answer(url)
        if answer is not None and answer[0] == 200:
            break
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            print(OPEN_YOURSELF.format(url=url))
            return
        time.sleep(POLL_SECONDS)
    if not _open(url):
        print(OPEN_YOURSELF.format(url=url))


def _port_range(raw: str) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """'FIRST-LAST' as argparse takes it, or exit 2."""
    first, sep, last = raw.partition("-")
    if sep != "-":
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ports must be FIRST-LAST, e.g. 8000-8010")
    try:
        first_port, last_port = int(first), int(last)
    except ValueError:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ports must be FIRST-LAST, e.g. 8000-8010")
    if not 1 <= first_port <= last_port <= 65535:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError("ports must be an increasing range within 1..65535")
    return first_port, last_port


def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
    """Pick a port, open the start page, and run the existing server. Returns its code."""
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="python3 tools/launch.py",
        description="Start the Ryde demo on the first free port and open the start page.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--ports",
        type=_port_range,
        default=(FIRST_PORT, LAST_PORT),
        metavar="FIRST-LAST",
        help="ports to try, in order (default: %(default)s)",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    first, last = args.ports

    port, already_running = pick_port(first, last)
    if port is None:
        print(NO_FREE_PORT.format(first=first, last=last))
        return 1

    url = start_url(port)
    if already_running:
        print(ALREADY_RUNNING.format(url=url))
        if not _open(url):
            print(OPEN_YOURSELF.format(url=url))
        return 0

    print(RUNNING.format(url=url))
    print(STOP_HINT)
    # The waiter must not run before the server, so it goes on a daemon thread and the
    # server keeps the main thread: Ctrl+C reaches app.server's own handler, and a
    # closed terminal window ends this one process and frees the port.
    threading.Thread(target=open_when_ready, args=(url,), daemon=True).start()
    return server.main(server_argv(port))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
"}

`git status --short` listed only the three allowed files before the commit and is empty after it. No file under `tests/` was touched.

**What changed** (3 files, +59/−6)
- `ui/switch-bar.css` — the three rules appended verbatim after the existing ones: the `body:has(.filing-shell #form-steps:not([hidden]))` column frame, `flex: none` on the bar, `flex: 1 1 auto; min-height: 0; height: auto; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box` on the shell, and the `max-height: 520px` hide rule. I diffed the appended block against the brief's fenced block programmatically: 30/30 lines identical, blank separator included, nothing else in the file touched.
- `tools/launch.py` — module-level `_opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))` now used by `_answer`; `PORT_TAKEN` plus an `OSError`/`errno.EADDRINUSE` (and `10048`) guard around `server.main(...)` that prints one line and returns 1, with every other exception re-raised; `CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 3.0` for the free-port `create_connection` while `PROBE_TIMEOUT` stays 1.0 for HTTP probes.
- `README.md` — the verbatim sentence `If you already started the demo yourself, the launcher reuses that copy as it is.` added directly after the sentence ending "uses the first free one."

**Extra verification beyond the suite:** served the filing pages from a manual server on 18500 and screenshotted them with the headless browser (DNS blocked, loopback exempt): at 1280×844 the bar sits above a full-height frame with the Continue button and fine print on screen for both the rider and driver forms; at 360×480 the bar steps aside and the form keeps its space; on `/party/status.html` at 360×480 the bar is back. Server stopped and port 18500 confirmed free.

Two notes: the earlier byte-level check that `ui/switch-bar.css` and `tools/launch.py` are absent from `FROZEN_W34` confirmed the allowed edits cannot trip the preservation pin. Separately, three orphaned `app.server` processes are bound to 18734–18736; they started at 23:54, 23:57 and 00:18 — before this fix round began — so they are not mine, and I left them rather than kill another process tree.
